method: Second source and control-flow review, independent of ML labels, earlier repository reviews, or external reputation. All sample bytes were SHA-256 verified. atomscan and cleave facts were run for every sample; final atomscan used this worktree with --no-update --mode slow --follow=none --format json. No PHP interpreter is installed; conclusions are static, not claims of observed execution. PHP single-quoted escape semantics were modeled to recover the exact written bytes. cleave flow is source-local may-flow and cannot prove runtime reachability or fully resolve extract().

Move the WordPress MU-plugin command composite from auth to request/command without changing its matcher, scope, criticality or proximity. Its description now states co-occurrence, not successful persistence.

Move php-system-request-source unchanged in scope and matcher to process/create/shell/command-string. Its description states source expression evidence; remove the webshell-specific ATT&CK default. Update all four YAML consumers and existing focused case references. This neutral source helper was the placement correction identified while reviewing the full 100-rule command leaf, which remains at 100 after the two moves.

consumer_audit: No exact consumers of the moved WordPress composite existed. The ancestor php-full-webshell composite separately requires auth and request facets: a command/write observation now supplies request only, and no target gains php-full-webshell. Webshell-wide selectors retain the WordPress composite and still have other request/command evidence where the neutral source helper moved out. Existing shell selectors gain the appropriately placed source expression, not a standalone conviction. Exact source-helper consumers preserve their previous evidence. File scopes and proximity limits are unchanged.

samples.identification_and_behavior: Standalone PHP request-controlled callable dispatcher, matching the Laudanum hidden-shell idiom; no family attribution is required. extract($_REQUEST) uses the default overwrite mode to create $ctime and $atime from request keys. The immediately following $ctime($atime) invokes the selected callable with the selected argument; die prints its return value and terminates. For example ctime=shell_exec and atime=printf CHECK select command execution and return its output. Both expressions use the @ error-suppression operator. There is no authentication or callable allowlist. Dynamic PHP callables are not eval(): eval is a language construct. No encoded or encrypted layer, outbound network destination, or persistence is present. Comments were not used to establish behavior.

samples.marker_note: PHP header-eval shell: reject quoted calls; allow header whitespace
samples.identification_and_behavior: Standalone PHP header-eval webshell. header() selects HTTP 404 but does not terminate execution. The next statement obtains X-Job from $_SERVER[HTTP_X_JOB], base64-decodes it and directly evaluates the decoded PHP in the current interpreter. An operator can encode arbitrary PHP statements, including shell commands, without any authentication or content check. The 404 response disguises an active endpoint. No payload is embedded: the encoded source is supplied at request time, so there are no embedded decoded executable strings to recover. The program is a reusable remote evaluation surface, not an ordinary missing-page handler.

samples.marker_note: WordPress command backdoor: fix placement and persistence claim
samples.identification_and_behavior: PHP command backdoor requiring a WordPress bootstrap that defines WPMU_PLUGIN_DIR. It builds a path to cache.php in that directory, writes a PHP command-shell string, then directly passes $_GET[cmd] to system(), which executes a shell command and emits output. No authentication, capability check, nonce or command allowlist exists. With ordinary warning handling a failed file write does not prevent the following command. The single-quoted payload preserves the backslashes before its double quotes: the generated file contains $_GET[\"cmd\"], which is invalid PHP syntax. Successful plugin persistence is therefore not established. If WordPress has not defined WPMU_PLUGIN_DIR, modern PHP aborts before either operation. The working command endpoint in its intended WordPress context is sufficient hostile behavior even though the attempted additional shell is broken.
